key_insight: An ultrathin oxide cap suppresses surface Sn exchange in SiGeSn, dramatically improving thermal stability during annealing.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to extend post-growth thermal budgets for SiGeSn-based silicon photonic and electronic devices.
method: In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry during 550 °C isothermal annealing
Compare uncapped vs oxide-capped Si0.08Ge0.83Sn0.04 films
Track thickness, composition, strain, and optical critical-point shifts
evidence_signal: After 50 min at 550 °C, uncapped films showed phase separation, 60% thickness loss, and a 400 meV E2 blueshift, while capped films changed by <1 at.% Sn and <20 meV.
watch_item: The oxide cap mainly blocks surface-mediated degradation, so bulk diffusion and process integration at higher temperatures may still limit device workflows.
paper_title: Enhanced thermal stability of SiGeSn by suppressing surface-mediated degradation
